Issued at 359 PM EDT Fri Aug 14 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Broad ridge axis over the central/northern Plains this morning, with 
troughing over the Western continent...and bits of energy amid 
broader troughing over eastern Canada, including a PV max over W. 
Ontario and a bit sliding by to our northeast through S. Ontario, 
resulting in upper confluence over the Great Lakes into the 
Northeast US. High pressure over central Canada beginning to ooze 
into the Upper Great Lakes, tapping into a cooler/drier continental 
airmass with prevailing/light northerly flow in the low-levels here 
in northern Michigan. (850mb temps in the 4-5C range to our 
northeast, with surface temps/dewpoints in the 45-55 range as of 
12z.) Meanwhile...to our south...pesky baroclinic zone remains stuck 
from the Central Plains into the OH Valley...with deep moisture 
(pwats of 2in or more and dewpoints in the 70s) pooling along the 
boundary...and nocturnal LLJ veering across the Plains to provide a 
source of forcing/instability. Have noted the westernmost convective 
complex shift from the Central Plains last night into IA early this 
AM and fading with time as the LLJ veers and the 700mb cap retreats 
southward with time...with additional convective complexes over 
IL/IN and WV as of 12-13z. 

Perturbation tracking through central Canada will result in 
increased return flow across the northern Plains/Upper 
Midwest...resulting in an area of pressure falls and precipitation 
to our northwest Saturday...while the BCZ to our southwest will 
remain in place and may also try to shift northward with time going 
into Saturday, with its own pressure falls and precipitation 
developing to our southwest...as moisture tries to sneak into the 
Upper Great Lakes, particularly Saturday night into Sunday, when our 
next best shot at rain will take place as that PV maxima treks 
across the region. This should exit stage right by Monday 
morning...with subtle ridging trying to build in for the day ahead 
of the next lobe of upper level energy tracking down out of central 
Canada. Currently, this appears to drag a boundary into the area for 
the midweek timeframe, which will be the next item of interest going 
forward. Beyond this...there are some signals for broad troughing to 
attempt to settle into the Upper Midwest/eastern continent, and 
ridging to try to build out west again. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/storm chances Saturday into Sunday... Dry low-level airmass 
currently funneling into the region from the north should slow top-
down saturation and precip chances late tonight into at least part 
of Saturday, with the best shot at activity across SW portions of 
our area (toward MBL) during the day. It wouldn't be entirely 
surprising if we were able to hold off a great deal, if not all, the 
rain chances till after dark Saturday, with the best shot at rain 
early Sunday morning as PV max and attendant surface low pass by to 
our north. Deep moisture does cross the area Sunday (pwats 1.5in or 
greater), but we may end up with relatively weak forcing 
overall...and do have to wonder if the better rain chances will 
focus themselves yet again over the Mid MS Valley/OH Valley (perhaps 
even as far north as southern MI?) where there is more potential for 
instability along the edge of the cap, which could rob us of some 
moisture...and perhaps set up potential for precipitation areas to 
split around parts of northern MI again. However, if that area does 
develop and does track into our area, which is not out of the 
question, would expect potential for significant rainfall totals 
over that portion of the area, especially as it would be more likely 
to train, and we expect to have anomalously high precipitable water 
values in the region (97-99th percentile vs climo). Greatest shot of 
this scenario would likely be near and south of M-55 (but most 
likely, well south). Otherwise...will look for some embedded thunder 
early Sunday morning, especially ahead of the cold front where there 
is a better shot at convective instability...and instability in 
general. Not impossible there could be some marginal deep-layer 
shear to work with during this timeframe that could try to organize 
any showers/storms, but we will see. 

Rain/storm chances look to return next week... Not impossible the 
weekend system allows a boundary to stall out over the Great Lakes 
region early next week, which should become important going into 
Tuesday as the next bit of energy slips down from Canada to 
reinforce that idea...perhaps with a bit of warm advection ahead of 
it? Or even some sort of MCS activity in the region with the ridge 
axis to our west. Attm, signals point toward a surface boundary 
draped across the Upper Midwest/Great Lakes by midweek, with some of
